newsitem.title: UK: EBRD sees 3.0 pct '97 GDP growth for E.Europe & CIS.
newsitem.headline: EBRD sees 3.0 pct '97 GDP growth for E.Europe & CIS.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) foresees growth of 3.0 percent in 1997 for Eastern Europe and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), EBRD first vice president Ronald Freeman told a conference on Saturday.
"While growth in 1996 lagged that of 1995, the outlook for the current year now looks better than for any year since the EBRD began operations in 1990," Freeman said.

He said the challenges for the region were to build capital markets, commercialise infrastructure and obtain market-friendly behaviour from the authorities which would allow competitive markets and private sector investment to develop and flourish.
"Some countries are still far from this last goal, demonstrating arbitrary measures, particulary in assessing taxes," he said, adding investors could not yet "effectively invest" in the region.
In 1996 the five best performing countries in GDP growth terms were Albanina, Georgia, Kyrgystan, Poland and the Slovak Republic.
"All had real GDP growth rates in excess of five percent," Freeman said. The five worst performers were Bulgaria, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan and Ukraine, all with negative GDP growth.

"In 1997 we continue to see Georgia with double digit GDP growth, in Poland and Slovakia growth slows and Albania -- where EBRD investments in the private sector had been performing well until the pyramid scheme debacle -- falls off any traceable growth curve," Freeman said.

He said Ukraine may remain in the negative column for 1997 although with slight signs of improvement, while Russia moved from negative to positive growth. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
